title: Proof Native Changes — System navigation, solid code

nativeImplementation.navigation: NavigationSplitView, balanced; sidebar List; segmented section picker
nativeImplementation.windowToolbar: System unified toolbar with navigationTitle(documentTitle); height and control geometry are system-managed, not fixed at 52pt
nativeImplementation.fonts: SF system / AppKit monospaced system font

materialPolicy.macOS26And27: System-provided navigation and toolbar Liquid Glass where supported; appearance and accessibility settings apply
materialPolicy.macOS13To15: Native compatibility appearance, not Liquid Glass
materialPolicy.code: Solid document background; no simulated blur or glass

nativeImplementation.motion: No added decorative entrance motion; retain system behavior and Reduce Motion

validation.status: Implementation documented; final native light/dark screenshot review and user approval not asserted
validation.required: Actual target-system app-window light/dark captures; record OS/SDK, capture method and illustrative Preview provenance

narrative.northStar: The review document leads; system navigation floats above it.
narrative.overview: User-requested macOS 27 Liquid Glass direction replaces the rejected CodeEdit-style icon rail and stacked gray bars. One native sidebar and a system unified toolbar frame a solid, legible diff document. Scope is the native Changes workspace only; Web/Tauri guidance is preserved.
keyCharacteristics: Human review remains distinct from Git staging

rules.name: Navigation material stops at code
rules.body: System glass belongs to navigation and controls, never the code document.

dos: Use native selection, keyboard focus, copy and find.
Preserve trust, confirmation, stale-write guards and cancellation.
Label illustrative data Preview and verify real app-window captures.
donts: Do not recreate the icon rail or stacked gray toolbar bands.
Do not fake glass with blur, images or translucent code.
Do not add third-party UI/editor dependencies.
Do not claim fallback systems are Liquid Glass or a build proves visual approval.
